descriptionChirho: Food, that which is eaten, solid nourishment. All 17 NT occurrences (Mt 14:15; Mk 7:19; Lk 3:11, 9:13; Jn 4:34; Rom 14:15, 20; 1 Cor 3:2, 6:13, 8:8, 8:13, 10:3; 1 Tim 4:3; Heb 9:10, 13:9) share uniform cross-linguistic translations: arb tacam/atcima, deu Speisen, fra nourriture, heb okhel/maakhal/mazon, hin bhojan, kor umsik, spa alimento/comida. The auto-clusters separated singular vs. plural forms, genitive vs. accusative cases, and the metaphorical 'solid food' of 1 Cor 3:2 (contrasted with milk for the spiritually immature). However, the metaphor is contextual rather than a distinct lexical sense; the word itself consistently denotes edible substance across all contexts including dietary regulations (1 Tim 4:3; Heb 13:9), literal provision (Mt 14:15; Lk 3:11), and doing God's will as food (Jn 4:34).
